gen-dafont-quantum-gf-quando: Quando reads bookish and traditional, a text serif spaced wide and sparse around a deep middle zone. But Quantum up top stays clean and loose, with no stroke contrast at all while the body has a little.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-amulya: Wide and geometric, Redux lets a big visible entrance lead into each curve, while Amulya keeps its curve gaps generous. Redux's heavier verticals against lighter horizontals give Amulya something to lean on.
gen-dafont-redux-fs-synonym: Redux sweeps a big entrance into every curve, with wide spacing and a gentle ebb and flow of weight. Synonym stays clean and dependable, its ink constant and every curve generously open, which grounds all that flourish.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-bree-serif: Contemporary and geometric, Redux comes in with big visible curve entrances. Bree Serif is literary and refined, its outsized lowercase making extended text feel generous, low in contrast and unhurried.
gen-dafont-redux-gf-quando: Geometric and wide-spaced, Redux arrives with confidence. Quando's bookish, traditional letters, with a deep middle zone and low contrast, give Redux's gentle modulation a grounded partner on the page.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-fs-quicksand: SF Wonder Comic is striking, its bowls left unfinished on one side. Quicksand's wirelike strokes of one thickness and terminals stopping short of the stem make extended reading feel light and approachable.
gen-dafont-sf-wonder-comic-gf-bree-serif: The body reads literary and refined, with outsized lowercase and low stroke contrast beneath the striking SF Wonder Comic heading. Bree Serif then carries extended text gently, leaving the dense, classic headline to do the shouting.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-plein: Plein is reliable and clean, with a clear channel opening the way to its rounded letters, a steady foil for Starborn. Starborn is ethereal and dreamy, best kept big and short.
gen-dafont-starborn-fs-synonym: Synonym is clean and dependable, its ink constant and its curves generously open, with no stroke modulation at all. And Starborn drifts in, dreamy and ethereal, with big blank gaps and a hint of modulation.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-almendra: Dreamy and spaced out, Starborn leaves big, blank gaps between its letters. Almendra, dignified and bookish, with a deep lowercase midsection, grounds that drifting heading firmly on the page.
